S.FORM: sua tia=kari=maku ia, tee=ku pu-isua navuŋ.
S.PHON: sua tiakarimaku ia teeku puisua navuŋ
S.FORM: sua tiakarimaku ia, teeku puisua navung.
S.PHON: sua tiaka[r|ɾ]imaku ia teeku puisua navuŋ
S.TRANSL: I am going to tell the story of a head (the one who had only a head).

S.FORM: sua piniŋ=kan ta-ʔaisi-a navuŋ ia, ni-mu-kusa=kan na cau pu-nannakə.
S.PHON: sua piniŋkan taʔaiʂia navuŋ ia nimukusakan na ʦau punannakə
S.FORM: sua piningkan ta'aisia navung ia, nimukusakan na cau punannake.
S.PHON: sua piniŋkan taʔaiʂia navuŋ ia nimukusakan na ʦau punannake
S.TRANSL: The head's neighbor (lit., the neighbor of where the head is i.e., lives) had gone to the people to arrange a marriage.

S.FORM: ni-m-ali-vali=kan sua cau-ini mu-vua ʔinia nannakə, ari-avic-ai=cu ʔinia nannakə iisa.
S.PHON: nimaɾivaɾikan sua ʦauini muvua ʔinia nannakə ariaviʦaiʦu ʔinia nannakə iisa
S.FORM: nimarivarikan sua cauini muvua 'inia nannake, ariavicaicu 'inia nannake iisa.
S.PHON: nima[r|ɾ]iva[r|ɾ]ikan sua ʦauini muvua ʔinia nannake a[r|ɾ]iaviʦaiʦu ʔinia nannake iisa
S.TRANSL: He took the girl away after her clansmen had agreed to give her to him.

S.FORM: ma-kasi=kan tanasa ta-ʔaisi-a navuŋ.
S.PHON: makaʂikan tanasa taʔaiʂia navuŋ
S.FORM: makasikan tanasa ta'aisia navung.
S.PHON: makaʂikan tanasa taʔaiʂia navuŋ
S.TRANSL: They came to the head's house (lit., the house where the head is).

S.FORM: "tupuru-a=cu, lavai," misa=kan ka-vaŋvaŋ maamia sua cau iisi ʔara-ʔaravaŋ.
S.PHON: tupuruaʦu ɾavai misakan kavaŋvaŋ maamia sua ʦau iiʂi ʔaraʔaravaŋ
S.FORM: "tupuruacu, ravai," misakan kavangvang maamia sua cau iisi 'ara'aravang.
S.PHON: tupu[r|ɾ]uaʦu [r|ɾ]avai misakan kavaŋvaŋ maamia sua ʦau iiʂi ʔa[r|ɾ]aʔa[r|ɾ]avaŋ
S.TRANSL: "Sit down now, lavai." Everyone inside (the house) said (to her).

S.FORM: "ʔaisi=cu nanu tia=laʔəv=aku," misa=kan sua nannakə.
S.PHON: ʔaiʂiʦu nanu tiaɾaʔəvaku misakan sua nannakə
S.FORM: "'aisicu nanu tiara'evaku," misakan sua nannake.
S.PHON: ʔaiʂiʦu nanu tia[r|ɾ]aʔevaku misakan sua nannake
S.TRANSL: "Where is my future husband?" the girl said.

S.FORM: ʔuuna=kan s<in>apar-a na tarəkəra=kan sua sikamə.
S.PHON: ʔuunakan ʂinapara na tarəkərakan sua ʂikamə
S.FORM: 'uunakan s<in>apara na tarekerakan sua sikame.
S.PHON: ʔuunakan ʂinapa[r|ɾ]a na ta[r|ɾ]eke[r|ɾ]akan sua ʂikame
S.TRANSL: A straw mat had been spread on the mortar.

S.FORM: "tupuru-a na iisi," misa=kan cau-ini.
S.PHON: tupurua na iiʂi misakan ʦauini
S.FORM: "tupurua na iisi," misakan cauini.
S.PHON: tupu[r|ɾ]ua na iiʂi misakan ʦauini
S.TRANSL: "Sit on this," said her people.

S.FORM: tupuru=kan ʔinia nannakə iisua.
S.PHON: tupurukan ʔinia nannakə iisua
S.FORM: tupurukan 'inia nannake iisua.
S.PHON: tupu[r|ɾ]ukan ʔinia nannake iisua
S.TRANSL: The girl sat there.

S.FORM: ʔacu=kan ni-paku-aluma maamia navuŋ r<um>aʔisi sua taaʔiica-ini.
S.PHON: ʔaʦukan nipakuaɾuma maamia navuŋ rumaʔiʂi sua taaʔiiʦaini
S.FORM: 'acukan nipakuaruma maamia navung r<um>a'isi sua taa'iicaini.
S.PHON: ʔaʦukan nipakua[r|ɾ]uma maamia navuŋ [r|ɾ]umaʔiʂi sua taaʔiiʦaini
S.TRANSL: All along she had been chased by the head and was bitten on the buttocks.

S.FORM: makasua=kan=cu raʔis-ai=cu ʔinia taniara.
S.PHON: makasuakanʦu raʔisaiʦu ʔinia taniara
S.FORM: makasuakancu ra'isaicu 'inia taniara.
S.PHON: makasuakanʦu [r|ɾ]aʔisaiʦu ʔinia tania[r|ɾ]a
S.TRANSL: Thereupon, she was bitten by it all day long.

S.FORM: ʔacu=kani=cu ʔuma-ʔuma cau ta-ʔaisi-a navuŋ.
S.PHON: ʔaʦukaniʦu ʔumaʔuma ʦau taʔaiʂia navuŋ
S.FORM: 'acukanicu 'uma'uma cau ta'aisia navung.
S.PHON: ʔaʦukaniʦu ʔumaʔuma ʦau taʔaiʂia navuŋ
S.TRANSL: The relatives in the head's house had gone to the rice fields.

S.FORM: tee=kan=cu mata-vəcəkai taniarə, ʔ<um>ucan=kan.
S.PHON: teekanʦu matavəʦəkai taniarə ʔumuʦankan
S.FORM: teekancu matavecekai taniare, '<um>ucankan.
S.PHON: teekanʦu mataveʦekai tania[r|ɾ]e ʔumuʦankan
S.TRANSL: When it was close to noon? (lit., when the sun would reach the meridian), it rained.

S.FORM: pu-a-kari-kari=kan sua nannakə, "paku-puli-au=pa=ku, tee=pa=ku ʔapi-sanuŋ ni-pa-ari-a" misa=kani sua nannakə.
S.PHON: puakarikarikan sua nannakə pakupuɾiaupaku teepaku ʔapisanuŋ nipaaria misakani sua nannakə
S.FORM: puakarikarikan sua nannake, "pakupuriaupaku, teepaku 'apisanung nipaaria" misakani sua nannake.
S.PHON: puaka[r|ɾ]ika[r|ɾ]ikan sua nannake pakupu[r|ɾ]iaupaku teepaku ʔapisanuŋ nipaa[r|ɾ]ia misakani sua nannake
S.TRANSL: The girl said, "Let me go! I have to bring back (the things) that are (out there) for drying in the sun."

S.FORM: paku-puli-ai=kan sua navuŋ.
S.PHON: pakupuɾiaikan sua navuŋ
S.FORM: pakupuriaikan sua navung.
S.PHON: pakupu[r|ɾ]iaikan sua navuŋ
S.TRANSL: The head let her go.

S.FORM: ma-caŋ-caŋarə=kan sua nannakə ma-ka-caŋ ara-takarə mu-caanə um-aŋuru.
S.PHON: maʦaŋʦaŋarəkan sua nannakə makaʦaŋ aratakarə muʦaanə umaŋuru
S.FORM: macangcangarekan sua nannake makacang aratakare mucaane umanguru.
S.PHON: maʦaŋʦaŋa[r|ɾ]ekan sua nannake makaʦaŋ a[r|ɾ]ataka[r|ɾ]e muʦaane umaŋu[r|ɾ]u
S.TRANSL: The girl was happy, (she) stood up immediately and ran away.

S.FORM: ala-sipalə=kan cakəran.
S.PHON: aɾaʂipaɾəkan ʦakəran
S.FORM: arasiparekan cakeran.
S.PHON: a[r|ɾ]aʂipa[r|ɾ]ekan ʦake[r|ɾ]an
S.TRANSL: She crossed the river.

S.FORM: apia-mau=kan, "hoo, iimukasu pulu-tumulu cakəran" misa=kani.
S.PHON: apiamaukan hoo iimukasu puɾutumuɾu ʦakəran misakani
S.FORM: apiamaukan, "hoo, iimukasu purutumuru cakeran" misakani.
S.PHON: apiamaukan hoo iimukasu pu[r|ɾ]utumu[r|ɾ]u ʦake[r|ɾ]an misakani
S.TRANSL: She made a wish, "Ho! May you the river be full of water."

S.FORM: tara-aiʔi=kan, ʔaisi=kan pari-viin ʔinia navuŋ.
S.PHON: taraaiʔikan ʔaiʂikan pariviin ʔinia navuŋ
S.FORM: taraai'ikan, 'aisikan pariviin 'inia navung.
S.PHON: ta[r|ɾ]aaiʔikan ʔaiʂikan pa[r|ɾ]iviin ʔinia navuŋ
S.TRANSL: As she looked back, the head was following her.

S.FORM: m-ala-susuna=kan navuŋ, "pita-kusa-u ʔikua vəcəraŋa=musu. tia=ta-pitu-kusa=maku" misa=kan.
S.PHON: maɾasusunakan navuŋ pitakusau ʔikua vəʦəraŋamusu tiatapitukusamaku misakan
S.FORM: marasusunakan navung, "pitakusau 'ikua vecerangamusu. tiatapitukusamaku" misakan.
S.PHON: ma[r|ɾ]asusunakan navuŋ pitakusau ʔikua veʦe[r|ɾ]aŋamusu tiatapitukusamaku misakan
S.TRANSL: The head shouted, "Throw me your headband! I want to (catch and) hold on to

S.FORM: paki-turu=kan sua nannakə pita-kusa ʔinia sua vəcəraŋa-ini.
S.PHON: pakiturukan sua nannakə pitakusa ʔinia sua vəʦəraŋaini
S.FORM: pakiturukan sua nannake pitakusa 'inia sua vecerangaini.
S.PHON: pakitu[r|ɾ]ukan sua nannake pitakusa ʔinia sua veʦe[r|ɾ]aŋaini
S.TRANSL: Willingly, the girl threw it her headband.

S.FORM: "mati-ʔələc-a" kisa-ən=kan=kiai.
S.PHON: matiʔəɾəʦa kisaənkankiai
S.FORM: "mati'ereca" kisaenkankiai.
S.PHON: matiʔe[r|ɾ]eʦa kisaenkankiai
S.TRANSL: "Catch it!" She said.

S.FORM: mata-atəa=kan vəla canumu, pati-puli-ai=kan ʔinia.
S.PHON: mataatəakan vəɾa ʦanumu patipuɾiaikan ʔinia
S.FORM: mataateakan vera canumu, patipuriaikan 'inia.
S.PHON: mataateakan ve[r|ɾ]a ʦanumu patipu[r|ɾ]iaikan ʔinia
S.TRANSL: As soon as (the head) reached the deep water, she released her headband.

S.FORM: makaran=kan na usur-ini sua navuŋ iisua.
S.PHON: makarankan na usurini sua navuŋ iisua
S.FORM: makarankan na usurini sua navung iisua.
S.PHON: maka[r|ɾ]ankan na usu[r|ɾ]ini sua navuŋ iisua
S.TRANSL: The head was carried by the currents to her fallow land.

S.FORM: makasua=kan=cu ma-ka-uali=kan musa=kan na usur-ini sua nannakə iisua.
S.PHON: makasuakanʦu makauaɾikan musakan na usurini sua nannakə iisua
S.FORM: makasuakancu makauarikan musakan na usurini sua nannake iisua.
S.PHON: makasuakanʦu makaua[r|ɾ]ikan musakan na usu[r|ɾ]ini sua nannake iisua
S.TRANSL: Shortly afterward, the girl went to her fallow land.

S.FORM: c<əm>əʔəra ʔaisi=kan ʔinia ni-ara-təmə taavu.
S.PHON: ʦəməʔəra ʔaiʂikan ʔinia niaratəmə taavu
S.FORM: c<em>e'era 'aisikan 'inia niarateme taavu.
S.PHON: ʦemeʔe[r|ɾ]a ʔaiʂikan ʔinia nia[r|ɾ]ateme taavu
S.TRANSL: She saw that a bottle gourd had been growing there.

S.FORM: pa-kari-ai=kan ʔinia cina-ini, "naini=kusa ʔinia ni-ara-təmə usuru=ta, cina, karanana ranəŋ-ini" misa=kani.
S.PHON: pakariaikan ʔinia tʂinaini nainikusa ʔinia niaratəmə usuruta tʂina karanana ranəŋini misakani
S.FORM: pakariaikan 'inia cinaini, "nainikusa 'inia niarateme usuruta, cina, karanana ranengini" misakani.
S.PHON: paka[r|ɾ]iaikan ʔinia tʂinaini nainikusa ʔinia nia[r|ɾ]ateme usu[r|ɾ]uta tʂina ka[r|ɾ]anana [r|ɾ]aneŋini misakani
S.TRANSL: She spoke to her mother, "What (kind of plant) has grown on our fallow land there, Mother, whose leaves are very different?"

S.FORM: mu-kusa=kan ʔinia mata cina-ini c<əm>əʔəra, taavu ava.
S.PHON: mukusakan ʔinia mata tʂinaini ʦəməʔəra taavu ava
S.FORM: mukusakan 'inia mata cinaini c<em>e'era, taavu ava.
S.PHON: mukusakan ʔinia mata tʂinaini ʦemeʔe[r|ɾ]a taavu ava
S.TRANSL: As she went there to see with her mother, it was in fact a bottle gourd.

S.FORM: makasua=kan=cu maka-vuŋavuŋ.
S.PHON: makasuakanʦu makavuŋavuŋ
S.FORM: makasuakancu makavungavung.
S.PHON: makasuakanʦu makavuŋavuŋ
S.TRANSL: Thereupon, it began to put forth a bud.

S.FORM: ma-ka-uali pu-aiʔi=kan ʔinia, takəpə=kan=cu.
S.PHON: makauaɾi puaiʔikan ʔinia takəpəkanʦu
S.FORM: makauari puai'ikan 'inia, takepekancu.
S.PHON: makaua[r|ɾ]i puaiʔikan ʔinia takepekanʦu
S.TRANSL: When she went back there shortly afterward, it was round already.

FORM.notes: Source parenthetical expanded under POL-026/POL-027; exact source and decision are in source_notation_audit.csv.

S.FORM: makasua=kan=cu pasi-kəəc-ənə=kani=kiai ha macuʔu taavu, kaʔan=kan=pa maa-maaraŋ.
S.PHON: makasuakanʦu paʂikəəʦənəkanikiai ha maʦuʔu taavu kaʔankanpa maamaaraŋ
S.FORM: makasuakancu pasikeecenekanikiai ha macu'u taavu, ka'ankanpa maamaarang.
S.PHON: makasuakanʦu paʂikeeʦenekanikiai ha maʦuʔu taavu kaʔankanpa maamaa[r|ɾ]aŋ
S.TRANSL: Thereupon, she pinched the fruit of the bottle gourd. It was not ripe yet.

FORM.notes: Source parenthetical expanded under POL-026/POL-027; exact source and decision are in source_notation_audit.csv.

S.FORM: makasua=kan=cu pasi-kəəc-ənə=kani=kiai sua macuʔu taavu, kaʔan=kan=pa maa-maaraŋ.
S.PHON: makasuakanʦu paʂikəəʦənəkanikiai sua maʦuʔu taavu kaʔankanpa maamaaraŋ
S.FORM: makasuakancu pasikeecenekanikiai sua macu'u taavu, ka'ankanpa maamaarang.
S.PHON: makasuakanʦu paʂikeeʦenekanikiai sua maʦuʔu taavu kaʔankanpa maamaa[r|ɾ]aŋ
S.TRANSL: Thereupon, she pinched the fruit of the bottle gourd. It was not ripe yet.

S.FORM: kaʔan=kan=pa apun-un=kiai.
S.PHON: kaʔankanpa apununkiai
S.FORM: ka'ankanpa apununkiai.
S.PHON: kaʔankanpa apununkiai
S.TRANSL: She did not pluck it yet.

S.FORM: pu-aiʔi=kan ʔinia masi-kəəcə, kaʔan=kan=pa maaraŋ.
S.PHON: puaiʔikan ʔinia maʂikəəʦə kaʔankanpa maaraŋ
S.FORM: puai'ikan 'inia masikeece, ka'ankanpa maarang.
S.PHON: puaiʔikan ʔinia maʂikeeʦe kaʔankanpa maa[r|ɾ]aŋ
S.TRANSL: She went back there again to pinch it. It was not ripe yet.

S.FORM: maka-una=kan ʔinia, kaʔan=kan=pa maaraŋ.
S.PHON: makaunakan ʔinia kaʔankanpa maaraŋ
S.FORM: makaunakan 'inia, ka'ankanpa maarang.
S.PHON: makaunakan ʔinia kaʔankanpa maa[r|ɾ]aŋ
S.TRANSL: She went there once again, it was not ripe yet.

S.FORM: maka-lava-lava=kan=cu ʔinia, maaraŋ=kan=cu.
S.PHON: makaɾavaɾavakanʦu ʔinia maaraŋkanʦu
S.FORM: makaravaravakancu 'inia, maarangkancu.
S.PHON: maka[r|ɾ]ava[r|ɾ]avakanʦu ʔinia maa[r|ɾ]aŋkanʦu
S.TRANSL: (When) she went there for the last time, and it was ripe already.

S.FORM: apun-ai ʔinia mu-tanasə.
S.PHON: apunai ʔinia mutanasə
S.FORM: apunai 'inia mutanase.
S.PHON: apunai ʔinia mutanase
S.TRANSL: She plucked it and brought it home.

S.FORM: pa-tupuru-ai=kan ʔinia na tarəkəra, m-ala-kulikuli=kan maamia.
S.PHON: patupuruaikan ʔinia na tarəkəra maɾakuɾikuɾikan maamia
S.FORM: patupuruaikan 'inia na tarekera, marakurikurikan maamia.
S.PHON: patupu[r|ɾ]uaikan ʔinia na ta[r|ɾ]eke[r|ɾ]a ma[r|ɾ]aku[r|ɾ]iku[r|ɾ]ikan maamia
S.TRANSL: When she seated it in the mortar, it kept rolling around.

S.FORM: patu-vali-ai=kan na tapu, m-ala-kulikuli=kan maamia mu-ca-caanə.
S.PHON: patuvaɾiaikan na tapu maɾakuɾikuɾikan maamia muʦaʦaanə
S.FORM: patuvariaikan na tapu, marakurikurikan maamia mucacaane.
S.PHON: patuva[r|ɾ]iaikan na tapu ma[r|ɾ]aku[r|ɾ]iku[r|ɾ]ikan maamia muʦaʦaane
S.TRANSL: When she shifted it to a pot stand, it kept rolling and moving away.

S.FORM: pa-tupuru-ai=kan na tapi, makasua=kan m-ala-kulikuli=kan maamia.
S.PHON: patupuruaikan na tapi makasuakan maɾakuɾikuɾikan maamia
S.FORM: patupuruaikan na tapi, makasuakan marakurikurikan maamia.
S.PHON: patupu[r|ɾ]uaikan na tapi makasuakan ma[r|ɾ]aku[r|ɾ]iku[r|ɾ]ikan maamia
S.TRANSL: She seated it into a basket. Thereupon, it kept rolling around.

S.FORM: patəʔa=kan sua nannakə iisua pa-tupuru ʔinia nakənakə tar-ini tanarau.
S.PHON: patəʔakan sua nannakə iisua patupuru ʔinia nakənakə tarini tanarau
S.FORM: pate'akan sua nannake iisua patupuru 'inia nakenake tarini tanarau.
S.PHON: pateʔakan sua nannake iisua patupu[r|ɾ]u ʔinia nakenake ta[r|ɾ]ini tana[r|ɾ]au
S.TRANSL: (Then) the girl came upon an idea and seated it (the bottle gourd) in a cool place under her bed.

S.FORM: tə-ʔələcə=cu.
S.PHON: təʔəɾəʦəʦu
S.FORM: te'erececu.
S.PHON: teʔe[r|ɾ]eʦeʦu
S.TRANSL: It stood still.

FORM.notes: Source parenthetical expanded under POL-026/POL-027; exact source and decision are in source_notation_audit.csv.

S.FORM: makasua=cu mu-caanə=cu mu-usa ʔuma-ʔuma.
S.PHON: makasuaʦu muʦaanəʦu muusa ʔumaʔuma
S.FORM: makasuacu mucaanecu muusa 'uma'uma.
S.PHON: makasuaʦu muʦaaneʦu muusa ʔumaʔuma
S.TRANSL: Thereupon, (the girl) left for the rice fields.

FORM.notes: Source parenthetical expanded under POL-026/POL-027; exact source and decision are in source_notation_audit.csv.

S.FORM: makasua=cu mu-caanə=cu mu-kusa ʔuma-ʔuma.
S.PHON: makasuaʦu muʦaanəʦu mukusa ʔumaʔuma
S.FORM: makasuacu mucaanecu mukusa 'uma'uma.
S.PHON: makasuaʦu muʦaaneʦu mukusa ʔumaʔuma
S.TRANSL: Thereupon, (the girl) left for the rice fields.

S.FORM: pu-aiʔi=kani tia=kan=cu tu-rua-rua-vana.
S.PHON: puaiʔikani tiakanʦu turuaruavana
S.FORM: puai'ikani tiakancu turuaruavana.
S.PHON: puaiʔikani tiakanʦu tu[r|ɾ]ua[r|ɾ]uavana
S.TRANSL: When she came home, it was getting late in the evening.

S.FORM: tan-cəʔəra=kan=cu tanasa, ca-canə, tara-kusa=kan na tanasa-ini, ni-putu-ʔənəv-a=kan si-ʔinəv-a-ini.
S.PHON: tanʦəʔərakanʦu tanasa ʦaʦanə tarakusakan na tanasaini niputuʔənəvakan ʂiʔinəvaini
S.FORM: tance'erakancu tanasa, cacane, tarakusakan na tanasaini, niputu'enevakan si'inevaini.
S.PHON: tanʦeʔe[r|ɾ]akanʦu tanasa ʦaʦane ta[r|ɾ]akusakan na tanasaini niputuʔenevakan ʂiʔinevaini
S.TRANSL: She saw the house from the road. As she looked at her house, its door was opened.

S.FORM: "cau=kusa ma-ka-nanu ni-putu-ʔənəvə=mita si ʔakia cau," misa=kan sua nannakə iisua.
S.PHON: ʦaukusa makananu niputuʔənəvəmita ʂi ʔakia ʦau misakan sua nannakə iisua
S.FORM: "caukusa makananu niputu'enevemita si 'akia cau," misakan sua nannake iisua.
S.PHON: ʦaukusa makananu niputuʔenevemita ʂi ʔakia ʦau misakan sua nannake iisua
